Recipe for those interested:

Mine:

  • 1lb of Best Malz Pilsen Malt
  • 1lb Weyermann Bohemian Pale Wheat Male
  • 3lbs Pilsen LME
  • 3lbs Wheat LME
  • ~.6oz of Magnum hope
  • 1oz of Styrian Goldings
  • ~10lbs blood orange juice/pulp
  • White Labs WLP565 Saison I Yeast

Pre-work Slice and pulp the meat from blood oranges until you have about 10lbs of glop. Based on my efforts it should take 15-18lbs of fruit ( I went through about 33lbs and got ~20lbs of pulp). Freeze it for a few weeks to make sure it's not going to cause an infection since we're not boiling it

  1. Grain to 190F for 20 min
  2. Add Extracts
  3. Magnum hops @ 60min
  4. Goldings @ 10 min
  5. cool and add yeast
  6. ferment for ~3weeks (this is your judgement, I got busy and didn't have time to transfer it sooner)

Racking to Secondary

  1. add blood orange ice blocks to secondary (did mine in a bucket instead of carboy
  2. rack on top of it
  3. I waited until the next day then added a second batch of yeast. May not be necessary, but I didn't know how the yeast would react to the ice.
  4. leave for another 2-3 weeks.
  5. Rack to tertiary and let settle (this helps to strain the pulp out - if you've another preferred straining method feel free to skip tertiary and bottle sooner)
  6. bottle it when you're ready!

Original Recipe I adapted this from (taken from an /r/homebrewing discussion

Sure.. this was published in Zymurgy a few years back, but the base recipe is for a pair of saisons. A blood orange saison and a Jasmine Green Tea Saison. I get bored of the same beer all the time, so I'll use my gear to brew 12-13 gallons of wort that I'll use to make multiple beers. In this case, I mashed and boiled the same - pitched two different strains and then flavored the beers differently at the end.

Jasmine Dragon Saison / Sangrael Saison

In my notes, I jokingly referred to this as the “Blood & Tea” Saison, which given the number of times the Wallonian countryside was fought over, makes sense. For the tea, buy a good quality tea like Adagio’s Jasmine Phoenix Pearls. For the blood oranges, hit the Farmer’s market in late January. If using regular oranges use less juice, it’s more acidic.

For 5.75 gallons at 1.059, 3.6 SRM, 6.6%ABV, 30 IBUs, 60 minutes boil

Malt / Grain / Sugar

  • 7.5 lbs Pilsner Malt
  • 4.0 lbs Wheat Malt
  • 0.5 lbs Flaked Wheat
  • 0.5 lbs Table Sugar

Mash

  • Single infusion – 150F for 60 minutes

Hops

  • 0.6 oz Magnum Pellets 12.9%AA 60 minutes
  • 1.0 oz Styrian Goldings 2.6%AA 10 minutes

Yeast (Jasmine Dragon)

  • Wyeast 3725 Biere de Garde

Yeast (Sangrael)

  • WLP565 Belgian Saison I

Extras (Jasmine Dragon)

  • ½ cup Tea Pearls
  • 1 cup Vodka
  • Soak for 3-5 days, checking on taste and color. Strain tea from vodka. Store and add to beer at packaging.

Extras (Sangrael)

  • 3 Blood oranges, zested introduced to whirlpool
  • 25 lbs Moro Blood Oranges, juiced (yielding ~3 liters of juice, frozen) – added during secondary

One thing I would say is that simply freezing the oranges won't necessarily going to prevent an infection. Freezing != sanitizing or sterilizing. Also, not trying to be a bigot or anything but is there a reason you didn't do all grain?

freezing - yeah, I understand that there is some possibility of an issue, but they were frozen solid for a bit over a month, so eh. plus it seems to have help burst any remaining fruit cells still hole from the light processing.

And I didn't do all grain because I don't have the equipment currently. I moved to SoCal last year and my tiny 800sqft apartment doesn't have much storage room for it. Hopefully that'll change going forward. I did have interest before the move, now I just don't have the space

I haven't done a whole lot with fruit but I'd probably done just the same as you. I did one fruit wine (strawberry) and did use campden tablets to sterilize the fruit before pitching the yeast. Definitely freezing allows the yeast to get at the sugars easier.
